subtitle: From Churulia’s Call to the Rebel’s Roar

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view, mid-shot, with swirling montage of mosque minaret, army camp, printing press and prison bars behind him
panels.action: Kazi Nazrul Islam stands defiant, pen in hand like a dagger, framed by faint silhouettes of Allah, Kali and Krishna rising together over a stormy Bengal landscape.

dialogue.text: He was a muezzin’s son, a soldier of empire, a jailed poet who sang Allah and Kali together—and set Bengal on fire with one word: Bidrohi.

i18n.hi: वो मुज़्ज़िन का बेटा, साम्राज्य का सिपाही, जेल में पड़ा कवि जिसने अल्लाह और काली को एक साथ गाया — और सिर्फ़ एक शब्द से बंगाल जला दिया: बिद्रोही।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of a dusty Bengal village at dawn
panels.action: Young Kazi Nazrul Islam walks barefoot along a narrow village path in Churulia, carrying a worn Quran and a small bundle, as a mosque and a thatched hut cluster in the mist.

dialogue.text: Churulia, 1899. In a poor village of Burdwan, a muezzin’s son learns the call to prayer, the ache of hunger, and the music of words, all in the same breath.

i18n.hi: चुरुलिया, 1899। बर्दवान के एक ग़रीब गाँव में मुज़्ज़िन का बेटा एक ही साँस में अज़ान, भूख का दर्द और शब्दों का संगीत सीखता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot inside a small mosque-room
panels.action: Nazrul, now a thin adolescent, stands on a simple wooden platform, hand to ear, calling the azan while a few villagers listen below, their faces lit by lamplight.

dialogue.text: He serves in the mosque, calls the azan, recites Arabic verses. But outside, in the akhara of village theatre, another call begins to pull at him.

i18n.hi: वो मस्जिद में सेवा करता है, अज़ान देता है, अरबी आयतें पढ़ता है। पर बाहर, गाँव के अखाड़े में चल रहे नाटक से उसे दूसरी पुकार खींचने लगती है।

panels.shot: energetic wide shot of a rural folk theatre stage at night
panels.action: Under oil lamps, Nazrul performs in a jatra troupe, dressed in costume, gesturing dramatically as villagers crowd close, spellbound by the mix of song and story.

dialogue.text: In the folk theatres he sings of kings, saints and lovers. Islamic tunes blend with kirtan cadences and baul wanderings. The boy from the mosque learns every tongue of Bengal.

i18n.hi: लोक नाटक में वो राजा, फ़क़ीर और आशिक़ों के गीत गाता है। इस्लामी सुरों में कीर्तन की ताल और बाऊल की भटकन घुल जाती है। मस्जिद का लड़का बंगाल की हर ज़बान सीख लेता है।

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot at a railway platform, steam swirling
panels.action: A teenage Nazrul, with a small cloth bag and determined eyes, steps toward a train marked with military insignia, British Indian soldiers milling around.

dialogue.text: Then war shakes the world. In 1917, still a teenager, Nazrul joins the British Indian Army, drawn by wages, adventure, and the road out of poverty.

i18n.hi: फिर जंग दुनिया हिला देती है। 1917 में, अभी किशोर ही, नज़्रुल मज़दूरी, रोमांच और ग़रीबी से निकलने की राह में ब्रिटिश इंडियन आर्मी में भरती हो जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in an army camp tent, lamplight and shadows
panels.action: Nazrul sits on a cot in a Karachi cantonment, rifle leaning nearby, scribbling in a notebook while other sepoys gamble or doze around him.

dialogue.text: Posted to Karachi, uniform on his shoulders, rifle by his side, he writes between drills. The empire trains his body; his mind quietly deserts to poetry.

i18n.hi: कراچي में तैनाती, कंधे पर وردी, पास में बंदूक, और ड्रिलों के बीच वो लिखता रहता है। साम्राज्य उसका जिस्म गढ़ता है, उसका दिमाग चुपके से शायरी में भाग जाता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up on Nazrul’s face, listening to distant bugles
panels.action: Nazrul looks out of the tent flap at a parade ground, the glow of sunset reflected in his eyes as bugles sound and a Union Jack flutters over marching lines.

dialogue.text: He sees drills, punishments, the arrogance of officers. The empire’s march beats in his ears—and something inside him beats back.

i18n.hi: वो ड्रिलें देखता है, सजाएँ, अफ़सरों का गुरूर। साम्राज्य की चाल की थाप कानों में गूंजती है — और भीतर से कुछ उसकी थाप को जवाब देता है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of post-war Calcutta street, crowded and alive
panels.action: Nazrul, now slightly older, steps into a bustling Calcutta lane with tram tracks, hawkers, posters and newspaper offices, clutching a rolled manuscript.

dialogue.text: After the war, he leaves the army and comes to Calcutta. Here, in a city humming with presses, protests and songs, the sepoy becomes a poet-journalist.

i18n.hi: जंग के बाद वो फौज छोड़कर कलकत्ता आता है। यहाँ छापाखानों, जलसों और गीतों से गूंजते शहर में सिपाही से कवि-संवाददाता बन जाता है।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot inside a modest newspaper office
panels.action: In a cramped room with piles of proofs and ink-stained tables, Nazrul leans over a desk, passionately reading out lines to a small group of fellow writers.

dialogue.text: He writes for journals, debates with editors, breathes in the anger of a colonised land. Bengal’s Muslims and Hindus both argue about identity; Nazrul writes past their lines.

i18n.hi: वो पत्रिकाओं के लिए लिखता है, संपादकों से बहस करता है, गुलाम मुल्क की घुटन अपनी साँसों में भरता है। बंगाल के हिंदू-मुस्लिम दोनों अपनी पहचान पर भिड़ते हैं, नज़्रुल उनकी लकीरों के पार लिखता है।

panels.shot: moody close-up of Nazrul’s hand writing, candlelight flickering
panels.action: Late night, Nazrul’s hand races over paper, words flowing as wax drips beside him; his face is tense, as if wrestling with an unseen storm.

dialogue.text: One winter night, his pen explodes. Line after line, he pours rage, myth, faith and defiance into a single long poem. He names it simply: Bidrohi—the Rebel.

i18n.hi: एक सर्द रात उसकी कलम फट पड़ती है। पंक्ति दर पंक्ति वो ग़ुस्सा, मिथक, ईमान और बगावत एक लंबी कविता में उँडेल देता है। नाम देता है बस इतना: बिद्रोही — बाग़ी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a small publishing office, men crowded around a fresh print
panels.action: In the Bijli magazine office, early 1922, Nazrul watches as sheets roll off a handpress, ‘Bidrohi’ occupying pages like a dense black river, while friends hover in awe.

dialogue.text: January 1922. Bijli prints Bidrohi. Bengal holds its breath as this young Muslim poet hurls Allah, Mahadev, Krishna and the thunder of revolt into the same burning song.

i18n.hi: जनवरी 1922। ‘बिजली’ में बिद्रोही छपता है। नौजवान मुस्लिम कवि अल्लाह, महादेव, कृष्ण और बगावत की गरज को एक ही धधकते गीत में फेंकता है, बंगाल साँस रोके सुनता है।

panels.shot: cinematic low-angle of Nazrul reciting to a small gathering
panels.action: Nazrul stands in a modest Calcutta hall, head thrown back, one hand raised as he recites passionately to an audience of mixed faiths, some shocked, some exhilarated.

dialogue.speaker: kazi_nazrul_islam
dialogue.text: “I am the rebel eternal, I raise my head beyond this sky!”

i18n.hi: "मैं अनंत बिद्रोही, ये आसमान फाड़ के सिर उठाता हूँ!"

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot of newspapers spread out on a table
panels.action: Various Bengali newspapers lie open on a table, headlines and columns visible, while Nazrul stands nearby, arms folded, watching as readers argue loudly in the background.

dialogue.text: The poem spreads like monsoon lightning. Some hail him as shair-e-islami, others as a blasphemer. Youth memorise his stanzas; elders mutter that he has gone too far.

i18n.hi: कविता मानसून की बिजली की तरह फैल जाती है। कोई उसे शाएर-ए-इस्लामी कहता है, कोई काफ़िर। नौजवान उसकी पंक्तियाँ ज़बानी याद करते हैं, बुज़ुर्ग बड़बड़ाते हैं कि ये हद पार कर गया।

panels.shot: gritty interior mid-shot in a different newspaper office
panels.action: In the Dhumketu office, Nazrul sits at a desk, face intense, as he writes a fiery editorial while an editor peers nervously through a window at a passing policeman.

dialogue.text: But Bidrohi is only the beginning. At Dhumketu, he turns his pen on the empire itself, writing of peasant suffering, police brutality, and the right to revolt.

i18n.hi: पर बिद्रोही बस शुरुआत है। ‘धूमकेतु’ में वो अपनी कलम सीधे साम्राज्य पर तान देता है — किसान की पीड़ा, पुलिस का ज़ुल्म और बगावत के हक़ पर लिखता है।

panels.shot: tense close-up of a printed Dhumketu issue being picked up
panels.action: A hand with a colonial-style cuff picks up a fresh copy of Dhumketu whose columns bristle with dense text, while in the background a constable stands to attention.

dialogue.text: The colonial censors read his words as sedition. In 1922, the British authorities move. For them, this poet’s metaphors are not just verse; they are a threat.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ी हुकूमत के सेंसर्स उसकी पंक्तियाँ ग़द्दारी पढ़ते हैं। 1922 में बहादुर सरकार हरकत में आती है। उनके लिए इस कवि की तश्बीहें सिर्फ़ शेर नहीं, ख़तरा हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic doorway mid-shot of arrest scene
panels.action: Nazrul stands in the doorway of a modest Calcutta lodging as uniformed Indian policemen, under a British officer’s gaze, step forward with a warrant, while curious neighbours watch.

dialogue.speaker: kazi_nazrul_islam
dialogue.text: “You can chain my body, not my song.”

i18n.hi: "मेरे जिस्म को बाँध सकते हो, मेरा गीत नहीं।"

panels.shot: somber wide shot of Alipore Jail exterior
panels.action: The high walls and gate of Alipore Jail loom under a grey sky as a line of prisoners is led inside; among them, Nazrul walks, head held steady.

dialogue.text: He is tried for sedition and sent to Alipore Jail. Bars and routines close around him, but prison only sharpens the edge of his rebellion.

i18n.hi: उस पर राजद्रोह का मुक़दमा चलता है और उसे अलीपुर जेल भेज दिया जाता है। सलाखें और दिनचर्या उसे घेर लेते हैं, पर क़ैद उसका बगावत वाला धार और तेज़ कर देती है।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot in a dim prison cell
panels.action: Inside a bare cell, Nazrul sits cross-legged on the floor, using his knee as a desk, writing intensely on sheets that pile beside him while a guard passes by the bars.

dialogue.text: In 1923, he writes Rajbondir Jabanbondi—the Statement of a Political Prisoner. It is not a plea. It is a manifesto, written from inside the empire’s cage.

i18n.hi: 1923 में वो लिखता है ‘राजबंदी की जबानबंदी’। ये दरख़्वास्त नहीं, साम्राज्य की सलाखों के भीतर से लिखा एक एलानिया इकरारनामा है।

panels.shot: close-up on Nazrul’s face as he recites his statement to an unseen court
panels.action: Nazrul stands, hands loosely bound, speaking with quiet fire toward an off-frame judge, while silhouettes of colonial officials listen in a darkened courtroom.

dialogue.speaker: kazi_nazrul_islam
dialogue.text: “I am with the oppressed, whether Hindu or Muslim, against every tyrant.”

i18n.hi: "मैं हर मज़लूम के साथ हूँ, हिंदू हो या मुसलमान, हर ज़ालिम के ख़िलाफ़।"

panels.shot: gentle wide shot of a simple Hindu household courtyard in 1920s Bengal
panels.action: Nazrul and Pramila Devi stand together under a leafy tree, hands just touching, while elders of both communities observe with varying expressions of curiosity, concern and quiet support.

dialogue.text: Released, he returns to song and struggle—and in 1924 marries Pramila Devi. A Muslim poet and a Hindu woman share a home, making his anti-communal ideals flesh.

i18n.hi: रिहा होकर वो फिर गीत और जंग-ए-कलम में लौटता है — और 1924 में प्रमिला देवी से निकाह/शादी कर लेता है। मुस्लिम कवि और हिंदू महिला एक घर बसाते हैं, उसकी सांप्रदायिकता-विरोधी सोच को जीते हैं।

panels.shot: warm interior mid-shot of Nazrul composing with harmonium and manuscripts
panels.action: Nazrul sits at a harmonium in a modest room, children’s toys scattered nearby, as he scribbles lyrics, his walls pinned with fragments of Bengali, Arabic and Sanskrit verses.

dialogue.text: His songs now move between ghazal and kirtan, Persian ghazal imagery and Krishna’s flute, Allah’s mercy and Kali’s dance of destruction. For him, these are not contradictions.

i18n.hi: अब उसके गीत ग़ज़ल और कीर्तन के बीच चलते हैं — फ़ारसी तसवीरें, कृष्ण की बाँसुरी, अल्लाह की रहमत और काली का तांडव एक धारा में बहते हैं। उसके लिए ये कोई टकराव नहीं।

panels.shot: lyrical wide shot of Nazrul singing before a mixed-faith audience
panels.action: In a town hall, Nazrul sings with eyes closed, harmonium before him, while Hindu and Muslim listeners sit side by side, some wiping tears, others nodding in time.

dialogue.speaker: kazi_nazrul_islam
dialogue.text: “If you split man by creed, you wound the One.”

i18n.hi: "इंसान को मज़हब से चीरोगे, तो एक ही को ज़ख़्मी करोगे।"

panels.shot: reflective mid-shot of older Nazrul looking at a printed book of his works
panels.action: Nazrul, now slightly greying at the temples, holds a bound collection of his poems, flipping through pages of Bidrohi and other works, as a window shows a changing city outside.

dialogue.text: By the early 1940s, illness will silence his voice. Yet the lines he wrote as a young rebel-soldier-poet keep marching, long after rifles and regimes have changed.

i18n.hi: 1940 के शुरुआती बरसों तक बीमारी उसकी आवाज़ छीन लेगी। पर जवान बाग़ी-सिपाही-कवि के लिखे अल्फ़ाज़ बंदूकों और हुकूमतों के बदलने के बाद भी चलते रहेंगे।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Nazrul’s statue or portrait in modern Dhaka or Kolkata
panels.action: A modern city street flows around a statue or portrait of Nazrul, schoolchildren, workers and elders passing by, some pausing, as clouds drift overhead.

dialogue.text: Kazi Nazrul Islam’s rebel cry rose from mosque and barrack, press and prison; it still asks each age whether its revolt will also refuse both tyranny and hatred.

i18n.hi: काज़ी नज़्रुल इस्लाम की बगावत की चीख मस्जिद, बैरक, प्रेस और जेल सब से उठी; हर दौर से पूछती है — तुम्हारी बगावत भी ज़ुल्म और नफ़रत दोनों को ठुकराएगी या नहीं।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Churulia’s Call to the Rebel’s Roar
subtitle_i18n.hi: चुरुलिया की पुकार से बागी की दहाड़ तक
